Read GPS CSV files into a single tibble

read_gps_csv.Rd

Reads subject-level GPS CSV files from a directory, matching filenames against a regex pattern and concatenating them into one tibble.

Usage

read_gps_csv(pattern, dir = NULL)

Arguments

pattern

Regular expression used to match filenames containing GPS data. Filenames must contain a subject ID like "Z001".

dir

Optional path to a directory containing the GPS files. If supplied, this overrides the GPS_SMB_ROOT environment variable. If not supplied, the function attempts to use the GPS_SMB_ROOT environment variable.

Value

A tibble with one row per GPS observation. Includes at least the columns subject, timestamp, lat, and (if present) lon. Additional columns are preserved.

Details

Each CSV must contain at least columns timestamp and lat, and either lon or lng. If a lng column is present, it is renamed to lon. A subject column is extracted from the filename using a regex pattern.

If both dir and the GPS_SMB_ROOT environment variable are missing or empty, the function will abort with an informative error.

Progress is displayed using the cli package.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Using GPS_SMB_ROOT set in ~/.Renviron
gps <- read_gps_csv(pattern = "^Z001.*\\.csv$")

# Or explicitly specify a directory
gps <- read_gps_csv(pattern = "^Z001.*\\.csv$", dir = "/path/to/gps_data")

} # }
